thread:
sara: heads up — customer 'acme-priv' reported a big perf regression after the onprem agent ran a kernel update overnight. pods failing with NCCL errors and lots of cudaInit() failures. can we triage?

ajay: on it. link to logs?

sara: pasted the kube logs below. appears right after host kernel package bumped to 5.15.120-rt.

sara: ```
I0318 03:21:07.123456 1 container.go:123] ERROR: cuda: cudaInit failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN
E0318 03:21:07.123789 1 nccl.go:87] NCCL_LOG: NET/IB transport failed: incompatible kernel module (abi mismatch)
```

linh: ^ that looks like the nv_peer_mem / ib_uverbs mismatch we've seen before. what's the nvidia driver reported on host?

mateo: ran remote check, customer host nvidia driver: 525.85.12, kernel version: 5.15.120-rt, nvidia-kmod built for 525.78.09 (so kmod ABI mismatch). nvidia-smi shows driver 525.85.12 but modinfo reports 525.78.09.

rebecca: ops-bot alert — node acme-node-07 marked degraded and drained automatically by autoscale-controller because health probe failures >3.

ops-bot: [automated] health-event: node acme-node-07 set to DRAINING at 2026-03-18T03:24:10Z; reason: kernel-module mismatch detected; remediation_suggested: rollback-host-kernel or recompile-nvidia-kmod.

ajay: customer says they applied a security kernel patch from their distro provider and insisted it was safe. they want us to add that kernel + kmod combo to our supported matrix so future runs don't fail. they claim other vendors work.

linh: adding arbitrary host kernels without validation is risky. we only support kernels we test against our pinned kmod ABI set + supported CUDA versions. we should offer two options: 1) vendor-suggested rollback to previous kernel (recommended), or 2) recompile the nvidia-kmod on their host (we can provide a script and guidance).

mateo: short-term workaround to keep inference online: force the pool to use GPU nodes with fallback driver-compatible images + set REDWOOD_ENABLE_CPU_FALLBACK=true in the deployment to avoid immediate crashes. but perf will take a hit.

sara: customer pushed back: "we can't rollback vendor security patch". they want a timeline for us to certify 5.15.120-rt. what's realistic?

linh: testing + kernel ABI validation: 2-3 business days to validate ABI compatibility, then rebuild and run full kernel-module smoke tests across our onprem harness. if all good, we can add to matrix. cannot be same-day.

ajay: ops question — do we accept customer recompiles as supported? if they build kmod against their kernel it may work but they'd be on their own if we can't reproduce.

rebecca: per policy, customer-built kmods are allowed but unsupported: we can offer guidance and a best-effort patch, but SLA/support requires we can reproduce in our lab or via their repro bundle.

mateo: suggested immediate steps for this thread: (1) provide customer with a "driver-check" preflight script they can run to detect kmod/driver/abi mismatches before kernel updates; (2) offer on-call window to help recompile kmod; (3) add kernel to our triage queue for formal validation.

ajay: +1 on driver preflight. make it blocking for our private deployment agent: if preflight fails, agent should refuse to apply kernel updates or at least warn and require opt-in. prevents silent drift.

linh: we already have a minimal check but it's coarse (checks nvidia-smi vs modinfo version). propose a more thorough script that checks:
- kernel version vs kmod build ABI (modinfo -F vermagic)
- presence of ib_*/uverbs kernel modules and their version
- CUDA toolkit compatibility table for runtime libs

linh: sketch of check: ```
#!/bin/bash
KVER=$(uname -r)
MODVER=$(modinfo nvidia | grep vermagic | awk '{print $2}')
if [[ "$KVER" != *"$MODVER"* ]]; then
  echo "DRIFT: kernel $KVER != nvidia kmod $MODVER"
  exit 1
fi
```

sara: can someone craft the preflight and a short support doc we can send to the customer? also want a canned policy note explaining why we can't instantly add kernels to supported matrix.

rebecca: i'll draft the support doc (customer-facing) with remediate steps + risks. aim for < 2 hours.

mateo: i'll prepare the preflight script and a non-invasive probe mode (--dry-run) that just reports mismatches. will attach instructions to run with sudo.

ajay: ops: do we need to open a formal "supported-matrix-dispute" ticket for product to decide policy? customer explicitly asked to be "guaranteed" for all vendor kernels; they have an enterprise contract clause that feels ambiguous.

rebecca: yes open a legal/psa ticket + include the customer contract clause. i can do that after doc draft.

linh: long term: we should consider a "driver-guard" feature in the agent that runs pre-update checks and optionally auto-builds kmods in a sandboxed container against the customer's kernel headers (requires headers available).

sara: agreed. for now: oj short plan: share preflight + support doc, offer recompile help, place this kernel on formal validation queue (ETA 3 business days). customer notified.

mateo: repro tip for SREs: if you see messages like "cudaInit failed: CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN" + "NET/IB transport failed: incompatible kernel module", start by checking modinfo/vermagic, then look for duplicate nvidia modules in /lib/modules and any DKMS remnants.

ajay: thx all. tagging @ops for monitoring during customer remediation. :eyes:

sara: closing the immediate alert — keeping the thread open for updates. :thumbsup:
